'''''Characteristic Classes''''' is a mathematical [[textbook]] about [[characteristic class]]es. It is considered a standard work for this topic.<ref name=":0" /> It was written by [[John Milnor]], who centrally used them in this construction of [[Milnor sphere]]s awarded with the [[Fields Medal|Field Medal]] in 1956,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-1962|title=Fields Medals 1962 - Hörmander & Milnor|access-date=2026-01-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Milnor|first=John|author-link=John Milnor|title=On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=64|number=2|date=1956|jstor=1969983|pages=399–405 |doi=10.2307/1969983 }}</ref> and [[James Stasheff]]. It was published on 24 August 1974.

== Content ==
''Characteristic Classes'' first gives a short introduction into [[vector bundle]]s and [[Cohomology|singular cohomology]],<ref>Milnor & Stasheff 74, Chapter 2, 3, 5, 6 und 7</ref> which characteristic classes connect. On this basis, the construction of the basic characteristic classes is described, which includes [[Stiefel–Whitney class]]es, [[Chern class]]es, [[Pontryagin class|Pontrjagin classes]] and the [[Euler class]].<ref>Milnor & Stasheff 74, Chapter 4, 8, 9, 14 und 15</ref> Afterwards, it descibres the applications, which includes those of [[Stiefel–Whitney number]]s and [[Pontrjagin number]]s for the classification of [[bordisms]].<ref>Milnor & Stasheff 74, Chapter 16 und 17</ref> It also describes minor characteristic classes like dual Stiefel–Whitney classes, integral Stiefel–Whitney classes, [[Wu classes]] and combinatorical Pontrjagin classes.<ref>Milnor & Stasheff 74, Chapter 20</ref> Central results like the [[Thom isomorphism]] and [[Hirzebruch signature theorem|Hirzebruch's signature theorem]] are also described.<ref>Milnor & Stasheff 74, Chapter 10, 18 und 19</ref>

== Background ==
In 1957, Jim Stasheff studied at [[Princeton University]], where John Milnor had obtained his [[PhD]] in 1954 and still continued to work. During a lecture from Milnor about characteristic classes, Stasheff wrote notes, which were later expanded and published as a textbook 17 years later. ("The text which follows is based mostly on lectures at Princeton University in 1957. The senior author wishes to apologize for the delay in publication."<ref name=":3">Milnor & Stasheff 74, Preface</ref>) [[Eduard Stiefel]], [[Hassler Whitney]], [[Shiing-Shen Chern|Shing-shen Chern]] and [[Lev Pontryagin|Lew Pontrjagin]] by then were all still active in research and the textbook was dedicated to them. ("We are happy to report that the four original creators of characteristic class theory all remain mathematically active. [....] This book is dedicated to them."<ref name=":3" />)

== Reviews ==
When John Milnor was awarded the [[Steele Prize]] in 2004, his works and contributions to mathematical literature were emphasized: His "ease is the mark of a master", so that an "improvement of Milnor's treatments often seems impossible". With this, he "set a standard of clarity, elegance, and beauty for which every mathematician should strive".<ref>{{Cite web|title=John W Milnor's awards|language=en|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Extras/Milnor_awards/|website=Maths History|access-date=2025-05-31}}</ref>

[[Edwin Spanier]] found the textbook "an elegant treatment of the subject". He wrote about any prior requirements: "The main concepts and results are lucidly presented and easily accessible. It is an excellent source for anyone who wants to learn or review the essentials of the subject." "The background is in algebraic and differential topology, differential geometry, algebraic geometry and global analysis." Even though the results come from mathematical physics, "background from physics is not given since it is not needed explicitly for the mathematical development". In summary, he concluded: "This book will be the basic reference. It will undoubtedly inspire future generations of mathematicians to attack some interesting and difficult questions."<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Spanier|first=Edwin|author-link=Edwin Spanier|title=Review: John W. Milnor and James D. Stasheff, Characteristic classes|journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=81|number=5|date=1975|pages=862–865|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1975-13864-X |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-american-mathematical-society/volume-81/issue-5/Review--John-W-Milnor-and-James-D-Stasheff-Characteristic/bams/1183537233.full?tab=ArticleLink|doi-access=free}}</ref>
